labels.notes: ers_corollary_4_73_secondCountable matches ers_corollary_4_73 (Causal/ErsUniqueness.lean:691) with exactly hmext and hthrough₂ removed and the SecondCountableTopology instance added. The only other difference is where the implicit {C} binder sits (a section variable in the original, after the instances here); it does not change the proposition. IsMDevelopment.isUniqueDevelopment_secondCountable matches the original (Causal/ErsMughd.lean:326) with exactly hmext and hthrough removed. The extra form ers_corollary_4_73_of_isCauchySurfaceOn_secondCountable replaces hacausal and hsplit with hC₁ : C.IsCauchySurfaceOn U₁ S and harc : C.CausallyArcConnectedOn U₁. I printed IsCauchySurfaceOn (every inextensible curve meets S exactly once) and CausallyArcConnectedOn (≤/≪ on every U ≤ W realised by causal/chronal curves): neither contains acausality or splitting as a conjunct. The proof term derives hacausal by IsCauchySurfaceOn.isAcausalOn_of_t1_secondCountable (from eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable, CurvesExtendSecondCountable) and hsplit by splitBy_of_t1_secondCountable (from splitBy_of_inextensibleThrough with InextensibleThrough proved). Both are therefore genuinely derived. harc is the ladder property causally_arc_connected, localised. No ladder rule derives it from globally_hyperbolic or tarentin, so it is not redundant. It is named in the docstring checklist and SCOPE and in the REPORT. This form is a sibling of the original, not ≥ it, and the REPORT presents it that way. The row stays partial and unmarked.

findings.what: The paper column of the checklist renders ERS's curve at ghd_02_19.tex:983 as 'a past inextendible g(u₂)-causal curve of U₂ through x'. The paper's curve is timelike, past directed, starts at x and is past inextendible. REPORT notes (9) tells the author that 'the curve ERS take at :983 … need[s] no Lorentzian input; on a T1, second countable background [it is a theorem] of the causal topology alone'. What inextensibleThrough_of_t1_secondCountable proves is an inextensible (two-sided, extension-defined) causal curve of U₂ through x, not a timelike one. That curve does the proof's job, because the Cauchy property makes it meet S, but it is not ERS's curve. The REPORT's own hypothesis row for this label states the paper's curve correctly ('g(u2)-timelike curve of U2 from x').
findings.fix: In the checklist row, keep the paper's wording (timelike, past directed, from x). Phrase the observation as: the curve the proof needs (an inextensible causal curve of U₂ through x, which meets S by the Cauchy property) exists on every T1, second countable background without Lorentzian input.

findings.what: The kb proposal says the three new lemmas 'discharge every hthrough, hthrough₂, hthroughτ and hsplit of NestedCausalities, ErsUniqueness and ErsMughd'. For the through-hypotheses this is right. For hsplit it is not. splitBy_of_t1_secondCountable needs S to be a Cauchy surface of the same W for the same causality, and most hsplit binders stand without such a hypothesis: Causal/ErsUniqueness.lean:405, 436, 469, 489, 597, 612, 636, 665, 694, 728, 755 and Causal/NestedCausalities.lean:1310 (ers_corollary_4_73's only Cauchy hypothesis on U₁ is for Cm). There hsplit is traded for IsCauchySurfaceOn, not discharged. The closer's own docstring (lines 35–37, 102–108) and ers_corollary_4_73_of_isCauchySurfaceOn_secondCountable say exactly that, as does T-abs-ers-4-64-second-countable's evidence. The kb line would mislead the next session.
